questions.question: Change the voice: Do you understand what I mean?

options.a: What I mean is that understood by you?
options.b: Was what I mean understood by you?
options.c: Is what I mean understood by you?
options.d: What I mean is understood by you?

questions.correct_answer_text: Is what I mean understood by you?
questions.explanation: Interrogative Active → Passive: the auxiliary moves to the front. Present Simple question → "Is ... understood by you?"

questions.question: Change the voice: Circumstances will oblige me to go.

options.a: I will oblige the circumstances and go.
options.b: I shall be obliged to go by the circumstances.
options.c: Under the circumstances, I should go.
options.d: I shall be obliged by the circumstances to go.

questions.correct_answer_text: Under the circumstances, I should go.
questions.explanation: "Circumstances will oblige me to go" → passive/idiomatic: "Under the circumstances, I should go."

questions.question: Change the voice: You need to clean your shoes properly.

options.a: Your shoes are needed to clean properly.
options.b: You are needed to clean your shoes properly.
options.c: Your shoes need to be cleaned properly.
options.d: Your shoes are needed by you to clean properly.

questions.correct_answer_text: Your shoes need to be cleaned properly.
questions.explanation: "need to + verb" → Passive: "need to be + past participle". Object (your shoes) becomes subject.

questions.question: Change the voice: You can play with these kittens quite safely.

options.a: These kittens can played with quite safely.
options.b: These kittens can play with you quite safely.
options.c: These kittens can be played with you quite safely.
options.d: These kittens can be played with quite safely.

questions.correct_answer_text: These kittens can be played with quite safely.
questions.explanation: Modal + active verb → Modal + be + past participle. "can play with" → "can be played with".

questions.question: Change the voice: You should open the wine about three hours before you use it.

options.a: Wine should be opened about three hours before use.
options.b: Wine should be opened by you three hours before use.
options.c: Wine should be opened about three hours before you use it.
options.d: Wine should be opened about three hours before it is used.

questions.correct_answer_text: Wine should be opened about three hours before it is used.
questions.explanation: Both clauses become passive. "you use it" → "it is used".

questions.question: Change the voice: Mona was writing a letter to her father.

options.a: A letter was written to her father by Mona.
options.b: A letter has been written to her father by Mona.
options.c: A letter was being written by Mona to her father.
options.d: A letter was written by Mona to her father.

questions.correct_answer_text: A letter was being written by Mona to her father.
questions.explanation: Past Continuous Active → Passive: Subject + was/were + being + V3. "was writing" → "was being written".

questions.question: Change the voice: Someone gave her a bull dog.

options.a: She was given a bull dog.
options.b: A bull dog was given to her.
options.c: She has been given a bull dog.
options.d: She is being given a bull dog by someone.

questions.correct_answer_text: A bull dog was given to her.
questions.explanation: Past Simple Active → Passive: Subject + was/were + V3. Indirect object (her) → "to her".

questions.question: Change the voice: A stone struck me on the head.

options.a: I was struck by a stone on the head.
options.b: My head was struck by a stone.
options.c: I had been struck by a stone on the head.
options.d: I was struck on the head by a stone.

questions.correct_answer_text: I was struck on the head by a stone.
questions.explanation: Past Simple Active → Passive. Adverbial phrase "on the head" stays in position: "I was struck on the head by a stone."

questions.question: Change the voice: He was arrested on the charge of theft, but for lack of evidence he was released.

options.a: He was arrested on a charge of theft, but was released for lack of evidence.
options.b: The police arrested him on a charge of theft, but for lack of evidence he was released.
options.c: The police arrested him on a charge of theft, but for lack of evidence released him.

questions.correct_answer_text: The police arrested him on a charge of theft, but for lack of evidence released him.
questions.explanation: Both passive clauses become active. Implied agent "the police" is used.

questions.question: Change the voice: I saw him conducting the rehearsal.

options.a: He was seen conducting the rehearsal.
options.b: I saw the rehearsal to be conducted by him.
options.c: He was seen by me to conduct the rehearsal.
options.d: I saw the rehearsal being conducted by him.

questions.correct_answer_text: I saw the rehearsal being conducted by him.
questions.explanation: Verb of perception (see) + object + V-ing → Passive: Subject + saw + object + being + V3.

questions.question: Change the voice: Have the box broken.

options.c: Get someone to break the box.

questions.correct_answer_text: Get someone to break the box.
questions.explanation: Causative "Have + object + V3" → Active equivalent: "Get someone to + base verb + object".

questions.question: Change the voice: The Romans expected to conquer Carthage.

options.a: Carthage was expected to be conquered by the Romans.
options.b: The Romans were expected to conquer Carthage.
options.c: It was expected by the Romans that they would conquer Carthage.
options.d: The Romans expected to have conquered Carthage.

questions.correct_answer_text: It was expected by the Romans that they would conquer Carthage.
questions.explanation: "Subject + expected + to + verb" → Passive: "It was expected by + agent + that + clause".

questions.question: Change the voice: Each member of the academy was given a prize.

options.a: Every member of the academy got a prize.
options.b: They give a prize to each member of the academy.
options.c: They are giving a prize to each member of the academy.
options.d: They gave a prize to each member of the academy.

questions.correct_answer_text: They gave a prize to each member of the academy.
questions.explanation: Past Simple Passive → Active: Subject (they) + V2 + object. "was given" → "gave".

questions.question: Change the voice: The thieves victimise the innocent commoners.

options.a: The innocent commoners had been victimised by the thieves.
options.b: The innocent commoners will be victimised by the thieves.
options.c: The innocent commoners are victimised by the thieves.
options.d: The innocent commoners were victimised by the thieves.

questions.correct_answer_text: The innocent commoners are victimised by the thieves.
questions.explanation: Present Simple Active → Passive: Subject + is/am/are + V3. "victimise" → "are victimised".

questions.question: Change into active form: 'I was surprised to see that he had been beaten black and blue.'

options.a: I was surprised to see he had been beaten black and blue.
options.b: It surprised me to see that he had been beaten black and blue.
options.c: It was surprising that he had been beaten black and blue.
options.d: That he had been beaten black and blue was surprising.

questions.correct_answer_text: It surprised me to see that he had been beaten black and blue.
questions.explanation: "I was surprised" (passive) → "It surprised me" (active). The subordinate clause remains.

questions.question: The active form of the sentence 'The visitors were shown a collection of old manuscripts.'

options.a: A collection of old manuscripts was shown to the visitors.
options.b: The hostess was showing the visitors a collection of old manuscripts.
options.c: The hostess showed the visitors a collection of old manuscripts.
options.d: The hostess was showed a collection of old manuscripts.

questions.correct_answer_text: The hostess showed the visitors a collection of old manuscripts.
questions.explanation: Past Simple Passive → Active: implied subject (the hostess) + showed + indirect object + direct object.

questions.question: Change the voice: He was congratulated by his teacher on his brilliant success in the recent examination.

options.a: He congratulated his teacher on his brilliant success in the examination.
options.b: His teacher congratulated him for his brilliant success in the recent examination.
options.c: His teacher congratulated him on his brilliant success in the examination.

questions.correct_answer_text: His teacher congratulated him for his brilliant success in the recent examination.
questions.explanation: Passive → Active: "by his teacher" becomes subject. "was congratulated" → "congratulated".

questions.question: You must do the work. (Change the Voice)

options.a: The work should be done by you.
options.b: The work must be done by you.
options.c: The work may be done by you.
options.d: The work might be done by you.

questions.correct_answer_text: The work must be done by you.
questions.explanation: With modal verbs in passive voice, the modal remains unchanged: modal + be + past participle. 'Must do' becomes 'must be done'.

questions.question: He helped me finish the work. (Make it passive)

options.a: I was helped by him for finishing the work.
options.b: I was helped for finishing the work by him.
options.c: I was helped by him to finish the work.
options.d: I was helped finishing the work by him.

questions.correct_answer_text: I was helped by him to finish the work.
questions.explanation: When 'help + bare infinitive' is made passive, the bare infinitive becomes 'to + infinitive'. 'Helped me finish' becomes 'was helped by him to finish'.
